BiblicalUsage: Patsa means to split, to wound. A prophet is smitten and wounded in 1 Kings 20:37, when the man of God tells his neighbour to smite him and the neighbour smites him and wounds him. In Song of Solomon 5:7 the watchmen that go about the city find the bride, smite her, and wound her, and take away her veil.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the wounding in these verses is the cost of obedience in one and the cost of searching in the other, and both are borne by people who did not turn back.
